title: Predictions for 5 biggest Morris/Sussex Week 8 football games | Exclusive - NewsBreak
text:
By Nick Gantaifis ,
18 hours ago
Here are five of the most compelling Morris/Sussex football games this week, along with analysis and predictions:
Old Tappan (7-0) at Montville (6-2) Friday, Oct. 23 6:30 p.m.
A rare regular-season finale between two Group 3 powers carries plenty of playoff implications as both teams look to solidify their postseason seeding.
Old Tappan has established itself as the team to beat in North Group 3, capturing sectional championships in each of the last two seasons. The Golden Knights enter the finale on the verge of a second consecutive unbeaten regular season, but Montville stands in their way. Old Tappan's offense revolves around dual-threat quarterback Zach Miceli, who has accounted for 2,083 total yards and 26 touchdowns. The senior has thrown for 1,588 yards and 17 scores while adding 495 rushing yards and nine touchdowns on the ground. His top target, Leo Etter, has 39 receptions for 675 yards and eight touchdowns, providing the Knights with one of North Jersey's most explosive passing connections.
The matchup lost a bit of its luster after Montville suffered a stunning setback to winless Morristown last week, but the Mustangs remain a dangerous postseason contender. Like Old Tappan, Montville is led by a dynamic quarterback-receiver combination. Jackson Gering has thrown for 1,134 yards and 14 touchdowns, directing an offense capable of striking quickly. Sophomore standout Andrew Baginski has emerged as one of the area's most versatile playmakers, totaling 926 yards from scrimmage and 16 touchdowns. Baginski has rushed for 364 yards and six scores while adding 32 receptions for 562 yards and 10 touchdowns.
Old Tappan is chasing perfection, while Montville looks to regain momentum and prove last week's upset was merely a bump in the road.
Prediction : Old Tappan 35, Montville 21
Vernon (5-3) at High Point (7-1) Friday, Oct. 23 6:30 p.m.
An all-Sussex County showdown takes center stage in Wantage with potential SFC American Blue title implications hanging in the balance.
Vernon enters the regular-season finale playing some of its best football of the year, having won three straight games and four of its last five. The Vikings have leaned on a dominant rushing attack and a stingy defense that has surrendered just 48 points during the three-game winning streak. Senior running back Andrew Geisen has been the catalyst, piling up 940 rushing yards and 17 touchdowns, while a ground-oriented offense has amassed nearly 2,400 rushing yards on the season.
Standing in the way is a High Point squad enjoying another outstanding campaign. The Wildcats are one victory away from completing a one-loss regular season and have extra motivation after Vernon denied them a perfect regular season a year ago. High Point's offense is powered by dual-threat quarterback Joey Elko, who has accounted for 1,588 total yards and 23 touchdowns, throwing for 858 yards and 10 scores while adding 686 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns. Defensively, the Wildcats have been equally impressive, allowing just 15 points per game.
Prediction : High Point 35, Vernon 24
West Morris (5-3) at Mount Olive (4-3) Friday, Oct. 23 6:30 p.m.
This year's renewal of the rivalry lacks some of the championship-caliber buzz it has carried in recent seasons, as both teams enter the regular-season finale searching for momentum after difficult stretches.
West Morris comes in stalled in a rare three-game skid, including a 19-16 loss to rival West Essex last week. The Wolfpack remain a physical, run-oriented team built around junior tailback Deacon Frayne, who has rushed for 1,206 yards and 16 touchdowns. While the offense has struggled to regain its early-season form, the defense has continued to make plays behind senior Brendan Dwyer, who has recorded 48 tackles and three interceptions, one of which he returned for a touchdown.
Mount Olive has endured a similar slide, dropping three of its last four contests following a 26-15 setback against Roxbury. The Marauders have battled injuries to several key contributors during that stretch, making consistency difficult to find. However, there was an encouraging sign last week with the return of senior running back Brayden Longo. After missing multiple games, Longo immediately provided a spark, rushing for 159 yards and showcasing his big-play ability on an electrifying 85-yard touchdown run.
Prediction : West Morris 21, Mount Olive 17
Boonton (7-1) at Mountain Lakes (4-4) Friday, Oct. 23 7 p.m.
This rivalry has largely belonged to Mountain Lakes, with Boonton’s last victory over its neighboring foe coming in 2018.
The Bombers, however, enter this year’s meeting enjoying their best season in five years under third-year coach Sean Norton. Powered by a dominant ground attack, Boonton has rushed for nearly 2,200 yards and 25 touchdowns, securing sole possession of the SFC National White title. Senior running back Josiah Chaplain III has been the catalyst, piling up 863 yards and 12 touchdowns.
Mountain Lakes is enduring an unfamiliar stretch. After opening the season 3-0, the Herd have lost four of their last five games, with several defeats coming by decisive margins. Despite the struggles, senior running back Jack Bronico remains one of the area’s top backs with 956 yards and 10 touchdowns, while quarterback Lawson Fagan has passed for 617 yards and six scores.
With Boonton surging and Mountain Lakes searching for answers, the Bombers have their best opportunity in years to reclaim bragging rights in this neighborhood rivalry.
Prediction : Boonton 28, Mountain Lakes 21
Pope John (2-5) at Delbarton (3-4) Saturday, Oct. 24 1 p.m.
All bets are off when Pope John and Delbarton renew their longstanding non-public rivalry. While neither team enters with the record it envisioned, the matchup still carries plenty of pride as the Green Wave look to extend their recent success against their Sussex County neighbors.
Pope John has endured a challenging season against one of New Jersey’s toughest schedules, dropping four of its last five games after a promising start. Offense has been hard to come by, with the Lions scoring just 73 points through seven games, while the defense has been tasked with carrying a heavy load. Senior running back Luke Gialanella has been a bright spot, leading the team with 288 rushing yards and three touchdowns.
Delbarton finds itself in a similar position. After opening the season with consecutive victories, the Green Wave have lost four of their last five contests while battling through a challenging slate of opponents. Junior transfer DJ Benfatti has emerged as one of the offense's most reliable playmakers, rushing for 309 yards and six touchdowns.
With both programs eager to build momentum heading into the postseason, expect a physical, hard-fought rivalry game between two proud programs looking to close out the regular season on a high note.
Prediction : Delbarton 34, Pope John 21
